Brick Wall

GeometryParadoxes
Game: This is a wall of straight, level rows of bricks. See whether the rows still look level when you slide the bricks about.
How to play: Drag the two dots under the wall, or use the sliders, to change the shift and the mortar. You can also focus a dot and use the arrow keys.
Look for the math

The surprising thing about this picture is how certain your eyes can be about something that is not true. The grey lines across the wall are drawn straight and level; nothing in the picture tilts them.

The lines are parallel

This is the café wall illusion, also called the brick wall illusion. Every mortar line is painted from the left edge to the right edge at one fixed height, and the next one is exactly one row lower. So the lines are truly parallel, whatever the sliders say. The logic test checks all 2,400 settings it tries against a second reading of the applet's own drawing code, and the lines are level in every one.

Why the rows look crooked

The bricks alternate between two shades, and every other row starts part of a brick across. At Shift = 50% the upright joints of one row land in the middle of the bricks in the next row. Your eye uses those upright joints as guide lines, and the level mortar lines appear to slope. Set Shift = 0% and the joints line up again: the test confirms that no joint crosses a row boundary then, while a half-brick shift makes plenty of them cross.

Mortar makes the tilt fade

The Mortar setting does not move the bricks. It only paints more grey lines on top of each row boundary: 2 × Mortar + 1 of them, from one thin line at 0 to twenty-one at 10. The original page says the illusion disappears as the mortar grows. That is a claim about what people see, so a computer cannot prove or disprove it; what the test can check is the geometry behind it — the grey band grows by two lines at every step and the lines stay level. Lowering the Shade slider brings the two brick shades closer together, which also weakens the effect.

The five settings, exactly as in the applet

Brick width and Row height are percentages of the wall's width and height, rounded down: Width = floor(canvasWidth × width% / 100). Shift is a percentage of a brick's width, Shift = floor(Width × shift% / 100). The first brick of an offset row starts far enough left that its joints interleave with the row below — the applet subtracts a whole brick until the x is not positive, then subtracts one more time. The greys are dark = max(0, (255 − Shade) / 2) and light = min(255, dark + Shade). The page renders these as blends of its own theme colours so the wall reads in both light and dark mode.

Try Shift = 50% with a thin wall and no mortar, then drag Mortar all the way to 10 and watch the slope fade away.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
